item.title: Israeli military says Hezbollah targets struck in Beirut
item.description: Israel says it targeted the Iran-backed armed group Hezbollah, as Tehran warns this could derail a US-Iran deal to end the fighting.

item.title: Is there an AI stock market bubble, and is it ready to burst?
item.description: Despite the Iran war, inflation and debt fears, US markets keep hitting record highs, fueled largely by AI. BBC's Samira Hussain looks into whether that bubble will burst.

item.title: One dead, five injured after shooting in Israel
item.description: The suspect opened fire from a car in several locations before being shot dead.

item.title: Iran's World Cup team lands in Mexico amid US visa row
item.description: All of Iran's group games are in the US, but players and support staff will have to fly in and out of the country on match day.

item.title: Russian families use AI to 'resurrect' loved ones killed in Ukraine
item.description: The highly controversial trend lies at the intersection of Russia's war on Ukraine, new AI technologies and grief.

item.title: The college scam that promised students fleeing war a new life in Finland
item.description: BBC speaks to students from war-torn Myanmar who say they were cheated after paying to study abroad.

item.title: Why the economics make this the craziest World Cup ever
item.description: From trade wars to soaring ticket prices, the 2026 World Cup is unlike any before it. Faisal Islam explores what this tournament reveals about our changing global economy.
